messages:
maria: Following up on the model rollout metadata thread. I sketched a concise resolution playbook that treats hints as 'soft inputs' and produces a single small resolved object for runtime. Goal: deterministic, testable, and observable.

sam: Nice. Can you drop the minimal resolved shape so runtime folks know what to expect?

maria: Resolved object (runtime-facing):

```json
{
  "effective_level": "low|medium|high",
  "effective_weight": "integer",
  "effective_origin": "client|route|tenant|global",
  "trace_id": "hex",
  "resolution_reason": "short string"
}
```

alex: Good. A couple things: 1) we need a deterministic precedence + tie-breaker rule, 2) a migration story for legacy 'anchor' and 'pin_strength' fields, and 3) telemetry budget for traces.

jamie: For precedence I propose: tenant_override (if mode=allow/block) > client > route > tenant-default > global. If two hints have same origin priority, pick higher weight. If weights equal, stable tie-breaker = origin_id lexicographic. Documented and unit-tested.

lee: Clarify tenant_override: block means absolute deny of lower-level hints, allow means always win, soft means we compare weights with a threshold. Example: tenant.weight=50, client.weight=65, tenant.soft_threshold=20 => 65-50=15 < 20 => tenant keeps control. If >= threshold, client wins. Default soft_threshold=20.

maria: Exactly. Also recommend a global safety_cap for weights (0..1000) so clients can't set extreme priorities. We'll validate at ingestion.

sam: Migration: map legacy fields at ingestion time: 'anchor' -> tenant_override.mode=allow with inferred expires_at=null, 'pin_strength' -> priority_hint.weight scaled into 0..100 range. Emit deprecation event and keep shim for 180 days.

alex: Observability: resolution_trace should be compact JSON string capped at 1024 bytes. Include applied_sources (list), chosen_rule, final_weight, and any clamped fields (e.g., capped weight). Redact tenant identifiers in trace unless sampled.

jamie: Metrics: gauge(effective_weight) per tenant, counter(override_mode_{allow|block|soft}), hist(resolution_latency_ms), sampled counter for full-resolution_trace. Also tag traces with route and model_id for debugging.

lee: Implementation notes: control-plane should expose a pure function resolve(hints, overrides, legacy) -> resolved_object + small_trace. Make this function deterministic and property-tested; run fuzz tests for conflicting hints.

maria: I'll add a small examples section to the RFC-followup PR showing TTL expiry:

Example: tenant_override expires in 1h; client escalates while override active -> client loses. After expiry, client reclaims based on weight. We'll include the snippet in docs.

sam: Can we add a sample CLI command to force re-resolve for a tenant after migration? ops likes quick remediation.

maria: Yes. CLI: `redwoodctl rollout resolve --tenant T123 --force` which will re-run resolution and emit an audit event. We'll add RBAC guard.

alex: Testing: add unit tests for every precedence permutation and an end-to-end canary run that compares old anchor semantics vs new resolved_object outputs for a sample tenant set.

jamie: Ops note: plan a 3% canary on Dedicated pools, monitor the effective_weight gauge drift and model affinity changes for 24h. Ops-bot will create the canary run after PR merge.

ops-bot: Canary job scheduled: canary/dedicated/3pct for PR#1250. Alert if >0.5% request reroutes to fallback model in 30m.

maria: Thanks. I'll draft the RFC patch with the resolution algorithm pseudocode, schema, migration shim plan (180d), telemetry tags, tests, examples, and CLI hook. Ping me if you want to be reviewer. :thumbsup:
